sources.title: Deletion vectors in Databricks
sources.reviewedEvidence: Deletion vectors record row modifications in metadata and readers apply them when resolving table state; logical removal can precede physical file rewrite.
sources.caveat: The core file-membership visual is a simplified table without deletion vectors. Support depends on client and operation; no feature is enabled or data purged.

sources.title: Rename and drop columns with Delta Lake column mapping
sources.reviewedEvidence: Column mapping supports metadata-only logical renames and drops without rewriting data files; non-additive changes can affect streaming readers and legacy path-based readers.
sources.caveat: Runtime, protocol, mapping mode and downstream limitations must be checked; no ALTER command is executed.

sources.reviewedEvidence: Change records include insert, delete, update_preimage and update_postimage labels plus a table commit version; preimage is before and postimage is after the update.

sources.reviewedEvidence: Incident response separates overall command, operational changes, communications and planning to coordinate work and avoid uncoordinated changes.
sources.caveat: Actual customer incident authority and procedures govern real response.

sources.title: Eliminating toil
sources.reviewedEvidence: Toil tends to be manual, repetitive, automatable operational work without lasting improvement and grows with service scale; not all unpleasant or administrative work is toil.
sources.caveat: No employer time-allocation target or automation guarantee is adopted.

sources.title: Postmortem culture: learning from failure
sources.reviewedEvidence: Concrete prioritized preventative actions and follow-through turn incident analysis into reduced recurrence or impact.
sources.caveat: The acceptance test below is original and synthetic, not evidence of a deployed fix.

sources.title: Forecasting
sources.reviewedEvidence: Forecasts are maintained estimates that use evolving system information; forecasting and budgeting are distinct, and variance feeds later decisions.
sources.caveat: No figures here are actual customer spending or authorization.

sources.title: Lakeflow Jobs
sources.reviewedEvidence: Jobs coordinates tasks and triggers, represents workflow dependencies and exposes task/run monitoring.
sources.caveat: Task status alone is not evidence of reconciled business state or exactly-once external effects.

sources.title: Configure task dependencies
sources.reviewedEvidence: Run-if conditions depend on upstream success, failure or completion; independent upstream work can execute in parallel.
sources.caveat: A completion condition is not the same as all prerequisites succeeding.

sources.title: Troubleshoot and repair job failures
sources.reviewedEvidence: Repair reruns unsuccessful/dependent tasks from their beginning using current settings; the documentation explicitly says Jobs does not make tasks idempotent.
sources.caveat: Review partial outputs and changed settings before repair. No cloud repair is executed in this course.

sources.title: Structured Streaming checkpoints
sources.reviewedEvidence: Checkpoints record per-query offsets, commits and state; deleting/changing location starts fresh, and each query needs its own location.
sources.caveat: Restart compatibility depends on query/source/state changes and runtime; not all changes support an old checkpoint.

sources.title: Use foreachBatch to write to arbitrary data sinks
sources.reviewedEvidence: foreachBatch supplies micro-batch output and batch identity; custom sink logic must address duplicate writes and failure handling.
sources.caveat: Custom external effects are not automatically exactly-once because upstream processing has checkpoints.

sources.title: Configure task dependencies
sources.reviewedEvidence: Run if condition options, notes: when every dependency is Excluded, the dependent task is also Excluded regardless of condition; exclusion cascades.
sources.caveat: Original hypothetical workflow or arithmetic, not an executed product test. Databricks Lakeflow Jobs on AWS; product behavior, not a configured customer job.

sources.title: Use task values to pass information between tasks
sources.reviewedEvidence: Set task values: JSON representation at most 48 KiB; set/get are Python notebook functions. Get notes discourage defaults that hide missing keys or wrong task names.
sources.caveat: Original hypothetical workflow or arithmetic, not an executed product test. Lakeflow Jobs task metadata; dynamic references are supported by tasks accepting parameters.

sources.title: Use foreachBatch to write to arbitrary data sinks
sources.reviewedEvidence: Completely consume each batch DataFrame: stateful queries must consume the full batch or restart; partial consumption can fail the next batch. The example contrasts show(2) with complete consumption.
sources.caveat: Original hypothetical workflow or arithmetic, not an executed product test. Structured Streaming with stateful operators and foreachBatch on Databricks; this is not a rule that every bounded batch query must collect all data.

sources.title: PySpark DataFrame quickstart, 4.0.4
sources.reviewedEvidence: Creation, column access, filtering, grouping and SQL sections distinguish typed lazy DataFrames, column expressions, actions and the shared SQL execution engine.
sources.caveat: Pinned local Spark 4.0.4. This is not a Databricks Runtime compatibility or production performance claim.

sources.title: Spark 4.0.4 NULL semantics
sources.reviewedEvidence: Comparison and aggregate sections distinguish unknown comparisons, explicit null checks, COUNT(*) and COUNT(column).
sources.caveat: Null-safe equality expresses a different rule; choosing it requires a business meaning for missing keys.

sources.title: Spark 4.0.4 JOIN reference
sources.reviewedEvidence: Inner joins combine matching rows; left-semi returns left rows with a match and left-anti those without one.
sources.caveat: Join type does not establish input key uniqueness or business grain.

sources.title: DataFrame.explain, 4.0.4
sources.reviewedEvidence: Explain API supports logical/physical plan views and formatted plan output.
sources.caveat: A planned operator is not observed runtime latency; adaptive execution can change plans.

sources.title: Python 3.12 data structures
sources.reviewedEvidence: Dictionary and iteration sections explain keyed records and traversal; a dictionary is not a declared tabular schema.
sources.caveat: Python 3.12 language reference, not a distributed execution model.

sources.title: Python 3.12 csv module
sources.reviewedEvidence: DictReader maps header fields to records; ordinary CSV reading returns strings and requires deliberate numeric conversion.
sources.caveat: CSV dialect and malformed-row policy remain application decisions.

sources.title: DataFrame.unionByName
sources.reviewedEvidence: unionByName aligns columns by name; allowMissingColumns=True fills absent fields with null. The API dates to 2.3 and the missing-column option to 3.1.
sources.caveat: Name alignment does not prove unit, meaning or type compatibility; optional extension only, no new execution claim.

sources.title: pyspark.sql.functions.explode_outer
sources.reviewedEvidence: explode_outer emits a row per array/map element and emits a null result for empty or null input, unlike ordinary explode.
sources.caveat: The operation changes output grain; a null placeholder is not a known list element. API dates to 2.3.

sources.title: Supercharge Data and AI Innovation with Azure Databricks — platform context
sources.reviewedEvidence: Reviewed Microsoft caption cues01:05–03:03: Azure service context, fragmented sources, Delta Lake and ADLS, then integrations. Caption source is the public video entry da09c909-a91f-42e6-becc-6f8c0784e1e2. Its October2025 hosting timestamp differs from the verified August12 original YouTube upload.
sources.caveat: A vendor overview, not deployment instructions. Do not adopt its promises of immediate feature availability or universal benefits; cloud, region and configuration still matter.

sources.title: Diving into Delta Lake Part1: Unpacking the Transaction Log — computing table state
sources.reviewedEvidence: The selected playback and caption review follows replay from a cached state through later JSON commits, then replacing that basis with a checkpoint plus later commits. The final portion introduces version/time travel. The publisher written companion was also reviewed. This is historical explanation, not a promise about current checkpoint cadence or retention defaults.
sources.caveat: Historical implementation illustration. Current protocol features, retention and VACUUM rules come from lesson documentation. A remove action is not proof of immediate physical deletion.

sources.title: AI-Powered Data Engineering Workflows: Positron for Databricks Users — inspect a join
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the join subsection:2016 trips versus2023 weather, hourly alignment and a local1000-row sample. Exact segment bounds were not exposed, so none are invented.
sources.caveat: The demonstration uses pandas and an AI assistant. It is not a PySpark execution proof, an instruction to install these tools, or evidence that generated joins are correct.

sources.title: Apache Spark Streaming and Delta Live Tables for real-time IoT insights
sources.reviewedEvidence: Reviewed the transcript passages on gaps/corrupted messages, Azure Event Hubs, bronze history for reprocessing, silver transformations and the downstream dashboard. The speaker explicitly identifies the demonstrated IoT input as simulated.
sources.caveat: A2023 case study using legacy Delta Live Tables terminology. Broad “exactly once” and cost-saving claims are not adopted; sink, checkpoint and business-key policies must be established separately. Exact architecture-segment bounds remain unverified.

sources.title: AI-Powered Data Engineering Workflows — from a local result to a scheduled job
sources.reviewedEvidence: Reviewed fetch-weather before dependent materialized views, configuration/deployment, and checks for datetime and temperature. No cloud execution was performed by this course.
sources.caveat: Tool demonstration, not a recovery guarantee. Retries require idempotent effects; dependency order alone does not make replay safe. Current bundle and pipeline names may differ.

sources.title: Apache Gluten: Revolutionizing Big Data Processing Efficiency — native operators and fallback
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read01:22–02:17 on Spark plugin control, native operator offload and fallback. Reviewed adjacent benchmark discussion to avoid presenting its speedups as universal. Event page dateMay21 differs from YouTube uploadMay29.
sources.caveat: Apache Gluten is not Databricks Photon. This is an explicitly different engine used to make execution boundaries visible. No quoted speedup, roadmap promise or Databricks equivalence is adopted.

sources.title: Supercharge Data and AI Innovation with Azure Databricks — governance responsibilities
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the Unity Catalog passage covering metadata, policies and lineage. The subsequent claim of ensured compliance is broader than the evidence and is explicitly excluded.
sources.caveat: Azure overview, not a security assessment. Unity Catalog does not by itself establish regulatory compliance, network isolation or every storage permission. Use the lesson’s current cloud-specific sources.

sources.title: MLOps with Databricks — a trained artifact versus predictions
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the artifact, batch-prediction and mixed lookup discussion; compared it with surrounding training/serving passages. Selected segment stops before specific online-table limitations.
sources.caveat: Practitioner guidance, not official Databricks commitments. Do not reuse nearby dated throughput limits or universal latency claims. This clip does not teach leakage or model validation; those remain in the authored lesson.

sources.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
sources.reviewedEvidence: The segment contrasts a confident response based on training with retrieving relevant documents, then shows a prompt containing instruction, retrieved context and the user question. The changing moon-count example is historical illustration, not a current astronomy claim. Retrieval does not guarantee correctness, freshness or authorization.
sources.caveat: RAG does not guarantee freshness, correctness, confidentiality or permission to act. The selected companion contains promotional guarantees that the course does not adopt. Permissions and separate evaluation remain necessary.

sources.title: Fivetran and Databricks CEOs — storage, compute and interoperability
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the separation/interoperability passage and the preceding explanation that data management involves more than files. The speakers are vendor executives; their competitive assertions are not neutral evidence.
sources.caveat: Do not infer universal interoperability, no lock-in or lower total cost. Verify protocol support, permissions, operational ownership and actual workload results. This is a claim to test, not an architecture verdict.

sources.title: The Meaning of Leadership
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full publisher transcript: owning failures, modeling behavior, empowering teammates and trusting people closer to the information. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/the-meaning-of-leadership-transcript.pdf
sources.caveat: General leadership conversation with Jonah Greenberger, Cody Karutz and Elaine Cheung; not a Databricks role or leveling rubric.

sources.title: The Customer Development Process
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full original transcript: hypotheses, external customer evidence, and learning about the problem rather than relying on friendly internal feedback. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/the-customer-development-process-transcript.pdf
sources.caveat: Steve Blank’s startup teaching from2008; the linked YouTube upload is2017. Apply the inquiry habit without presenting startup advice as enterprise qualification policy.

sources.title: Supercharge Your Pitches with Storytelling
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full Stephanie Lampkin publisher transcript; reviewed the three-question structure and her personal storytelling context. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/supercharge-your-pitches-with-storytelling-transcript.pdf
sources.caveat: Founder-pitch advice adapted to demo narrative. Its general memory/brain assertion is not used as a scientific claim; narrative must not conceal limitations.

sources.title: Four Ways to Validate an Idea
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full Adam Pisoni transcript: distinct value, monetization, distribution and friction hypotheses; narrow experiments before committing to a build. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/four-ways-to-validate-an-idea-transcript.pdf
sources.caveat: Startup framework adapted to enterprise experimentation. The transcript mistranscribes monetization as modernization; revenue anecdotes are not evidence for this course’s ROI.

sources.title: Mapping Customer Pains to Value Proposition
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full original two-page transcript: customer jobs/pains/gains, the offer, and the need to explain fit between them. Transcript: https://ecorner.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2012/01/2880.pdf
sources.caveat: Alexander Osterwalder with Steve Blank; general value-design guidance. Lecture dateJan26 differs from YouTube uploadFeb6. No vendor ranking or guaranteed ROI follows.

sources.title: How to Identify Your Priorities
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read the full Adam Pisoni transcript: a prioritization criterion, critical hypotheses, resource constraints and stopping when the most pressing constraint changes. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/how-to-identify-your-priorities-transcript.pdf
sources.caveat: The Yammer growth anecdote is context, not a universal goal. For this course, prioritize customer risk and agreed evidence rather than growth at any cost.
